title: Safepoint-driven node lifecycle automation for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets require predictable throughput guarantees and safe maintenance that avoid p99/p95 latency regressions during node lifecycle events. Current drain/upgrade workflows are ad hoc: full-drain or immediate eviction can cause transient capacity loss and tail latency spikes. We need an automated, observable lifecycle controller ('Safepoint Controller') that coordinates node states (active, marked-for-drain, safepoint, drained, reprovision) with autoscaler and routing layers to honor throughput SLAs and maintenance windows.
goals: Implement a Safepoint-driven state machine to declaratively move nodes through lifecycle stages with progress checkpoints
Coordinate with autoscaler so capacity reservations and proactive scaling prevent throughput violations during drains/upgrades
Add maintenance-window awareness and prioritized draining rules (by instance type, GPU occupancy, pinned customers)
Provide operator-facing commands and console UI hooks for previewing safepoint impacts and aborting drains
Ship telemetry hooks: safepoint latency, in-flight token eviction rate, KV cache warmup time, and throughput headroom metrics
acceptance_criteria: Can mark a node for safepoint and see a staged countdown with predicted throughput impact
Autoscaler maintains >= configured throughput_headroom during phased drains in 95% of synthetic traffic tests
Console shows per-node safepoint state and expected completion ETA
Graceful drain completes without evicting >5% of active requests per safepoint across production-like testbed
implementation_notes: High-level approach: 1) Add safepoint annotation to node objects and expose a controller that enforces per-node checkpoints (drain-window, cache-commit, connection-quiesce). 2) Autoscaler integration: preemptively increase reserved_capacity and establish a temporary routing weight shift to compatible model variants. 3) Eviction policy: soft-evict long-running streams with backoff and force-evict only after safepoint timeout. 4) Maintenance windows: allow schedule-based safepoint initiation and emergency path that short-circuits to emergency-drain with alerting. 5) Provide dry-run/simulate mode for operators and a CLI: redwoodctl node safepoint --simulate.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: KV cache warming vs immediate reclaim: we prefer staged cache release to avoid huge latency spikes; this increases total drain time but reduces p99 spikes
Throughput guarantees: implement 'throughput_headroom' config per pool instead of hard reservation to allow temporary burst scaling and better cost efficiency
Rolling upgrades vs bulk replacement: choose rolling with overlapping headroom to minimize customer impact even when upgrades take longer
progress_updates: 2026-02-11: Spike completed to evaluate safepoint annotations and controller patterns. Prototype controller reconciler created in infra/fleet (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4890).
2026-02-20: Autoscaler contract defined: new RPC 'ReserveCapacity(pool, tokens)' added to autoscaler API. Draft PR: github.com/redwood/autoscaler/pull/132.
2026-02-28: Integration test harness for synthetic traffic launched; initial run shows 12% throughput dip during naive drain. Identified need for 20% headroom config for affected pools.

2026-03-05: Design review with PM & SRE. Action items: add dry-run, expose safepoint ETA in console, and create operator abort flow. Recorded notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/2539-Design+Review+Notes
2026-03-10: Implementation: added soft-evict path and safepoint timeout. End-to-end in staging shows improved p99 but increased total drain duration by ~35%.
2026-03-12: QA test suite expanded to include heterogeneous instance mixes and pinned-tenant workloads. Next: add console wiring and run a canary on a dedicated non-production fleet.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Torres): Ensure safepoint ETA uses historical warmup curves per model to avoid optimistic estimates.
SRE (Daniel Park): Add alert thresholds for when autoscaler ReserveCapacity RPC latency exceeds 500ms; prefer synchronous fail-fast for emergency drains.
Design (Maya Chen): Console should visualize node safepoint phases with color-coded steps and an 'impact simulator' overlay.
qa_plan: Run staged chaos exercises: scheduled drains during steady traffic, during ramp, and emergency drains. Measure throughput, tail latency, and failed request counts. Validate autoscaler reserve/scale actions and ensure no customer-facing 5xx increases beyond baseline.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind fleet.experimental.safepoint; 2) Dry-run on internal dev fleets; 3) Canary rollout to a single non-production dedicated tenant for 72 hours; 4) Controlled rollout across low-risk pools; 5) Full rollout with 24h watch + on-call SRE for first two weeks.
operator_docs: Confluence: Fleet Operations -> Safepoint Controller Runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/2610-Runbook
notes: Next blockers: finalize autoscaler RPC contract (edge cases for concurrent safepoints), and determine default throughput_headroom per pool based on model mix. Follow-up ticket to add per-tenant pinned-reservation and billing implications (PM to scope).
